source_user: Define KV cache and explain one reason it matters in LLM infrastructure. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: Definition: A KV cache stores the attention keys and values computed for earlier tokens so autoregressive decoding can reuse them instead of recomputing the entire prefix at every output step. Mechanism: at decode step t, the new query attends to cached K/V for positions 1..t; only the new token's K/V is appended. This reduces repeated prefix compute and usually lowers per-token latency, but it consumes memory proportional to layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, batch/concurrency, and bytes per element. Boundary condition: the cache is useful only while the request's prefix remains active and fits the chosen memory budget; long contexts or high concurrency can exhaust GPU memory, requiring paging, quantization, eviction, or a lower concurrency limit. State actual latency and memory effects from measurements for the model, batch shape, and hardware rather than assuming them.

source_user: Give two failure modes or trade-offs associated with KV cache. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: During autoregressive decoding, cached keys and values avoid recomputing prior tokens; memory grows with layers, sequence length, KV heads, head dimension, and bytes per value.
corrected_answer: Two trade-offs are important. First, memory pressure: each generated token appends K/V for every layer and KV head, so long contexts and concurrent requests can exhaust device memory; paging or eviction may avoid an OOM but adds transfers and latency. Second, cache reuse is conditional: a cache can be reused only when the tokenized prefix and relevant model/adapter state match; otherwise using it would produce incorrect attention results. A concrete failure mode is stale or incorrectly keyed entries after a model-version, tokenizer, tenant, or sampling-context change. Boundary condition: the direction and size of the trade-off depend on precision, paging policy, context length, batch shape, and concurrency, so a single benchmark is not general evidence.

source_user: Define prefill and explain one reason it matters in LLM infrastructure. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Prefill processes the prompt and is generally parallel across prompt tokens; its cost is dominated by prompt processing and often compute utilization.
corrected_answer: Definition: prefill is the initial forward pass over the input prompt before generated tokens are decoded. Unlike sequential decode, prompt-token computations can generally be parallelized within a batch, and the pass produces the initial KV cache. Mechanism: the model processes the prompt in one or more parallel kernels, writing keys and values that the decoder will consume. This matters because it often determines time-to-first-token and can use compute efficiently, while prompt length and attention implementation affect memory traffic and cost. Boundary condition: parallelism is limited by available memory, batch shape, padding, and any prefix-cache reuse; a long or heterogeneous batch may not behave like an ideal dense workload. Claim improvement only after measuring TTFT/prefill latency, prompt tokens/s, compute utilization, HBM bandwidth, peak memory, and tail latency on the target model, precision, sequence lengths, and hardware.

source_user: Contrast prefill with a naive implementation that does not use it. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Prefill processes the prompt and is generally parallel across prompt tokens; its cost is dominated by prompt processing and often compute utilization.
